sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the opposite party no.2 filed Maintenance Case No. 254 of 2019, wherein on the intervention of the family members of the respective parties, the dispute between the parties was amicably settled and there was a joint compromise dated 26.08.2022 whereby the parties have settled their dispute.
A joint compromise petition was filed before the Family Court, Deoghar in Maintenance Case No. 254 of 2019, the copy of which is annexed as annexure -4 of this criminal miscellaneous petition.
It is next submitted that in view of the compromise between the parties, the chance of conviction of the petitioner is remote and bleak.

It is lastly submitted that the Complaint Case No.
1224 of 2019 and order taking cognizance dated 07.02.2020 whereby cognizance has been taken under Section 325/342/498A/504/34 of the Indian Penal Code be quashed and set aside.

4. The learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer to quash the Complaint Case No. 1224 of 2019 and order taking cognizance dated 07.02.2020 whereby cognizance has been taken of the offences punishable under Section 325/342/498A/504/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is next submitted that the petitioner has gone back from the compromise and has practiced fraud upon the trial court and keeping in view the misconduct of the petitioner and his criminal intent, as undisputedly the offences in respect of which cognizance has been taken by the learned court below is made out against the petitioner, hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.
5.

The learned Addl. P.P. on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer for quashing the Complaint Case No. 1224 of 2019 and order taking cognizance dated 0 7 . 0 2 . 2 0 2 0 w h e r e b y c o g n i z a n c e h a s b e e n t a k e n u n d e r S e c t i o n 325/342/498A/504/34 of the Indian Penal Code and submits that a private purported compromise which is denied by the opposite party no.2 cannot be a ground for quashing the entire criminal proceeding when undisputedly the offences made against the petitioner is made out on the basis of the materials available in the record.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

6. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, the undisputed fact remains that the materials in the record are sufficient to constitute the offences of which cognizance has been taken by the learned Magistrate.
The only ground upon which quashing of the complaint case and the cognizance order is sought, is that there was a compromise but the said compromise is denied by the opposite party no.2.

In view of the categorical denial of the opposite party no.2 about the compromise claimed by the petitioner, this Court is of the considered view that there is insufficient material in the record to suggest that in fact, any compromise has been entered into between the petitioner and the opposite party no.2.

Further if at all, there is any compromise, the complainant may Vikas Kumar @ Vikas Srivastava vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191274555/
2 not prosecute the complaint.

sentences.text: But when undisputedly the offences of which cognizance has been taken by the learned Magistrate is made out against the petitioner and the compromise itself is in dispute, this Court do not find any justifiable reason to quash the Complaint Case No. 1224 of 2019 and order taking cognizance dated 07.02.2020 whereby cognizance has been taken under Section 325/342/498A/504/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
7. Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is dismissed.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated the 10th June, 2024 AFR/Sonu-Gunjan/-
